This creates multiple integration seams for auth/readiness instead of one explicit handoff point.

issues.summary: No automated test harness exists for production code paths
issues.suggestion: Add a test runner (Vitest or Jest), define `npm test`, and establish baseline suites for Convex domain/runtime modules before further feature work.
evidence: `package.json` defines no `test` script and repository scan finds no test files (`.test/.spec/__tests__`).
This removes regression protection for all runtime paths, including mission progression and command processing.

issues.summary: Critical mission progression mutation logic has zero direct unit tests
issues.suggestion: Create focused unit tests around `validateAndPrepareUpdate` and `validateMissionStepInternal` covering all status and branching combinations with explicit assertions on `changes` payload and `result`.
evidence: `validateAndPrepareUpdate` controls step advancement, completion status, feedback, and skill awards.
No unit tests verify key branches: non-in-progress status, empty plan, step mismatch, step match, and mission completion transitions.

issues.summary: No integration tests verify command-to-mission progression across module boundaries
issues.suggestion: Add integration tests with mocked/fake Convex context that execute representative command flows and assert mission progress docs, output lines, and skill-point updates together.
evidence: `gameActions.sendCommand` and async finalization paths call `validateAllMissionsInBatch`, coupling command execution to mission progress persistence.
There are no cross-module tests asserting that a command updates mission progress, terminal output feedback, and skill points coherently in one flow.

issues.summary: Timestamp generation is hard-coded, encouraging brittle assertions
issues.suggestion: Inject a clock function (defaulting to `Date.now`) into mission update helpers so tests can pass fixed timestamps and assert exact persisted values reliably.
evidence: `validateAndPrepareUpdate` uses `Date.now()` directly for `completedSteps[].timestamp` and `completedAt`.
Without injected clock control, deterministic tests require global time mocking and become fragile.

issues.summary: Sibling mission lookup helpers encode not-found as different shapes (`undefined` vs `[]`).
issues.suggestion: Standardize lookup contract across mission helpers (for example: return a shared `Result`/discriminated union with explicit `not_found` vs `no_plan`, or keep nullable return semantics consistently) and update callers to one predictable pattern.
evidence: `getMissionById(missionId)` returns `MissionSpec | undefined`.
`getMissionPlan(missionId)` internally calls `getMissionById` but returns `mission?.optimalPlan ?? []`, collapsing missing mission and no-plan into the same `[]` result.

issues.summary: One module imports the same API family from both barrel and subpath entrypoints.
issues.suggestion: Define and enforce one public import surface for domain spec helpers (prefer the barrel or prefer subpath), then normalize existing imports to that single convention.
evidence: `convex/missions.ts` imports `getMissionPlan`/`matchesStep` from `./domainSpec` and `getMissionsForRoom` from `./domainSpec/runtime`.
`convex/domainSpec/index.ts` re-exports `runtime`, so both import routes are valid and competing.

issues.summary: Related mission APIs use inconsistent failure channels (throws vs status-like returns).
issues.suggestion: Choose a consistent error contract for mission APIs at boundaries (typed thrown errors with codes, or discriminated return objects) and document it in exported function/mutation contracts so callers can handle failures uniformly.
evidence: `gameActions.startMission` throws `Error` for mission-not-found and unavailable-room conditions.
`validateMissionStepInternal` and `validateAndPrepareUpdate` represent invalid states as normal return payloads (`matched: false`, feedback text), not thrown errors.

issues.summary: Heavy JSDoc blocks restate obvious behavior on short helper functions
issues.suggestion: Trim JSDoc to only non-obvious constraints and boundary behavior; keep short one-line summaries for simple helpers and remove tutorial-style examples unless they document edge cases.
evidence: `getMissionById`, `getMissionPlan`, and `hasPlan` are small/readable functions but each has long `@example/@returns` sections.
`requireAuth` and `requireAuthWithPlayerId` include tutorial-style doc blocks that mostly paraphrase function signatures.
`convex/gameData.ts` adds multi-paragraph module and export comments for direct data mappings.

issues.summary: Wrapper functions add indirection while only delegating to existing logic
issues.suggestion: Inline or remove pure delegation layers where no policy/telemetry/caching is added; if compatibility is required, consolidate wrappers into a single compatibility module with clear deprecation timeline.
evidence: `validateMissionStep` internal mutation only forwards arguments to `validateMissionStepInternal` and returns the result.
`validateAllMissionSteps` is deprecated and only delegates to `validateAllMissionsInBatch`.
`requireAuthWithPlayerId` is mostly a wrapper around `requireAuth` plus one subject check.

issues.summary: Many comments narrate exact code steps without adding why/constraints
issues.suggestion: Replace restating comments with rationale-only notes (business rule, non-obvious invariant, planner constraint). Move long format/tutorial guidance to external docs and keep file-local comments minimal.
evidence: Comments like `// No active missions`, `// Validate all in memory`, `// Apply all patches` mirror adjacent statements in `convex/missions.ts`.
`convex/utils/cacheUtils.ts` uses explanatory comments for straightforward operations (`Count active threats`, `Simple hash function`) already obvious from code.
`pddl/planning.ts` includes an extensive format tutorial in-file instead of concise, actionable local constraints.

issues.summary: Repeated defensive try/catch + console.error blocks add noisy boilerplate
issues.suggestion: Extract shared action error-handling utility (or higher-order wrapper) that standardizes logging and fallback shaping; keep handlers focused on core operation logic.
evidence: `cleanupCacheEntriesInternal`, `cleanupCacheEntries`, and `getCacheStats` each repeat similar `try/catch`, `console.error`, and default fallback returns.
Error paths are nearly templated and could be centralized.

issues.summary: Deprecated mission-validation mutation remains exported alongside the replacement API.
issues.suggestion: Remove `validateAllMissionSteps` after confirming no external/internal callers depend on it; if temporary compatibility is required, add a tracked removal issue/date and route all callers through one canonical API until deletion.
evidence: `convex/missions.ts` defines `validateAllMissionSteps` with `@deprecated Use validateAllMissionsInBatch directly` but still exports it as an internal mutation.
`convex/gameActions.ts` already imports and uses `validateAllMissionsInBatch` directly, indicating the new path is active while the old shim remains.

issues.summary: Both barrel and direct-file imports coexist for domainSpec APIs.
issues.suggestion: Standardize on one import surface (prefer the barrel if intended as the public module boundary), export missing symbols there if needed, and update call sites to eliminate mixed old/new access patterns.
evidence: `convex/missions.ts` imports `getMissionPlan`/`matchesStep` from `./domainSpec` and `getMissionsForRoom` from `./domainSpec/runtime` in the same module.
`convex/gameData.ts` uses barrel import `./domainSpec`, while `convex/gameActions.ts` imports from `./domainSpec/runtime`.

issues.summary: Migration-era comment references an old module without closure metadata.
issues.suggestion: Replace migration-history phrasing with current-state contract docs, or annotate with a tracked issue/date if migration cleanup is still pending.
evidence: `convex/gameData.ts` documents: `This replaces the old utils/GameData.ts for backend usage.`
The comment gives no migration status, removal tracking, or compatibility constraints, so it reads as leftover migration context rather than current contract.

issues.summary: The `convex/` root mixes config, contracts, and gameplay workflows in one flat layer.
issues.suggestion: Stage reorg in three moves: (1) create folders `convex/config/` (auth/convex config), `convex/contracts/` (schema/types), and `convex/functions/game/` + `convex/functions/ops/` (gameplay vs maintenance actions); (2) move files in order: config files first, then contracts, then operational/game files (`cacheCleanup.ts`, `missions.ts`, `gameData.ts`, `gameActions.ts`) to minimize temporary broken imports; (3) run import updates and validation with `rg -n "from \"\./(auth\.config|convex\.config|schema|types|gameActions|gameData|missions|cacheCleanup)\"" convex app components lib scripts`, then `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm lint`.
evidence: Top-level `convex/` currently holds 8 production files spanning unrelated ownership boundaries (platform boot/config, shared contracts, gameplay state/actions, maintenance actions).

Structure profile marks this directory as disproportionately large (`total_loc: 1911`) and only lightly reused per file (`avg_fan_in: 1.0`), which indicates search-first navigation instead of predictable placement.

issues.summary: Path conventions for domain-spec are split between current and legacy package roots, reducing discoverability.
issues.suggestion: Apply a staged docs/package clarity cleanup: (1) define a single canonical map in `docs/ssot/README.md` for `convex/domainSpec/` (runtime source) and `pddl/` (planner build artifacts); (2) update legacy `packages/domain-spec` references across docs to current paths using `rg -n "packages/domain-spec|packages/domain spec" docs scripts README.md`; (3) add a short root-level `docs/architecture/package-map.md` and validate consistency with `rg -n "convex/domainSpec|pddl/" docs README.md` plus a dry run of planner flow `pnpm planning:refresh`.
evidence: `convex/domainSpec/index.ts` and runtime imports treat `convex/domainSpec/` as canonical, but multiple docs still direct contributors to `packages/domain-spec/...` paths.
This creates a navigation mismatch between implementation and guidance, especially around `pddl/` vs `convex/domainSpec/pddl/` responsibilities.

issues.summary: Convex client is constructed at import time from env, creating fragile boot coupling.
issues.suggestion: Move client creation behind a lazily initialized provider-local factory (e.g., `useMemo` or a `getConvexClient()` helper) that validates env explicitly and throws a clear runtime error only when provider is actually rendered.
evidence: Line 8 constructs `new ConvexReactClient(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL!)` at module load.
The non-null assertion (`!`) means missing env fails only after import-time construction path is reached, which is brittle in tests/alternative runtimes.

issues.summary: Agent singleton is instantiated at module scope, coupling runtime behavior to import order.
issues.suggestion: Introduce an explicit `getPingAgent()` factory/registry that lazily creates and caches the Agent, and inject it into `executePingCommand` (or retrieve from a scoped runtime context) so initialization is intentional and overridable.
evidence: Line 61 exports `pingAgent` as `new Agent(...)` at module scope.
Action handler reuses this singleton (`pingAgent.continueThread` / `pingAgent.createThread`), so tests and alternate boot paths cannot easily control initialization or replace dependencies.

issues.summary: Auth provider domain is bound from environment at module initialization time.
issues.suggestion: Export a `buildAuthConfig()` function that reads env at call time and validates required keys, then call it from the Convex bootstrap entrypoint to make initialization order explicit.
evidence: The exported `authConfig` object includes `domain: process.env.CLERK_JWT_ISSUER_DOMAIN` directly in module scope.
This creates boot-time coupling to environment loading order and makes config mutation/testing harder without reloading the module.

issues.summary: gameActions.ts is a multi-domain orchestration hub with mixed concerns
issues.suggestion: Split gameActions into focused modules: (1) command dispatch/execution, (2) output/game-state finalization, (3) mission-facing public API, and keep only thin Convex handlers in gameActions.ts delegating to those modules.
evidence: convex/gameActions.ts (~975 LOC) contains command parsing helpers, sync command rendering, async tool orchestration, cache logic, mission entrypoints, and game-state persistence in one file.
Both transport-layer concerns (scheduler/action wiring) and domain concerns (mission/game progression) are implemented side-by-side in the same module.

issues.summary: Command output+mission+state update flow is duplicated across execution paths
issues.suggestion: Introduce a single shared finalization routine used by cache-hit and async-complete paths (or route both through finalizeCommandOutput) with one canonical mission-feedback/output/state-update sequence.
evidence: In sendCommand cache-hit branch, code validates missions, merges feedback into output lines, inserts/patches output, then updates skill points/tool session.
finalizeCommandOutput repeats the same structural sequence (mission validation, output assembly, terminal patch, state patch), creating parallel implementations of the same orchestration contract.

issues.summary: GameTerminal component mixes UI composition with orchestration state machine
issues.suggestion: Extract a dedicated hook (e.g., useTerminalSessionController) for initialization/state-machine logic and a single command router function reused by both manual submit and nav-triggered execution.
evidence: GameTerminal owns auth/loading guards, server initialization effects, scroll effects, nav hover policy, mission modal state, and command dispatch decisions.
Mission command branching is duplicated in both handleSubmit and executeCommand, indicating command-routing logic is spread across handlers instead of centralized.

issues.summary: Internal/admin cache cleanup handlers repeat identical operational flow
issues.suggestion: Factor shared cleanup execution into one private helper that both actions call, keeping auth checks at entrypoints and one canonical result-mapping implementation.
evidence: cleanupCacheEntriesInternal and cleanupCacheEntries each perform the same mutation call and identical success/error result shaping.
Only auth gating differs, but the cleanup behavior itself is duplicated rather than delegated.

issues.summary: initialRoom is typed as Room but can resolve to undefined at runtime
issues.suggestion: Make the contract honest by either (a) changing the type to `Room | undefined` and handling it at call sites, or (b) enforcing a guaranteed fallback with an explicit runtime guard (throw with clear error) or a constructed default Room object.
evidence: convex/gameData.ts:67-68 exports `initialRoom: Room = rooms[runtime.domain.rooms[0]?.id ?? "server-room"]`.
If `runtime.domain.rooms` is empty and `rooms["server-room"]` is absent, the lookup returns `undefined`, violating the declared `Room` contract and docstring fallback claim.

issues.summary: Fallback branch checks impossible condition when extracting cache hash
issues.suggestion: Remove the unreachable fallback and directly slice after the last colon (or return hash separately from `generateCacheKey` to avoid string parsing entirely).
evidence: pingAgent.ts uses `lastColon === -1 ? cacheKey : cacheKey.slice(lastColon + 1)` after `generateCacheKey(...)`.
cacheUtils.ts `generateCacheKey` always formats as ``${command}:${target}:${Math.abs(hash).toString(36)}``, guaranteeing at least one colon.

issues.summary: Same missions-command branch is duplicated across two handlers
issues.suggestion: Extract mission-command handling into one helper (e.g., `handleSpecialCommand(command)`), and call it from both handlers so command branching logic exists in one place.
evidence: `handleSubmit` checks `input.trim().toLowerCase() === "missions"` and opens the mission panel.
`executeCommand` repeats the same check and behavior, creating parallel control paths for one command.

issues.summary: Auto-scroll effect includes a dead local variable and no-op statement
issues.suggestion: Delete the `lines` variable and `void lines;` no-op; keep the effect keyed by `renderedOutput.length` only.
evidence: Effect defines `const lines = renderedOutput.length;` then uses `void lines;` with no behavioral impact.
The dependency is already `renderedOutput.length`, so this local variable does not contribute to control flow.

issues.summary: Room map construction uses an assertion that bypasses shape checking
issues.suggestion: Type `runtime.domain.rooms` at the source to match `Room` (or use a runtime validator) and remove `as Room` so assignment is type-checked directly.
evidence: `rooms` is built with `acc[room.id] = room as Room;`, so mismatches between `runtime.domain.rooms` and `Room` are hidden from the type system.

issues.summary: initialRoom is typed as Room even though indexed lookup may be undefined
issues.suggestion: Either guarantee existence with an explicit guard/throw before assignment, or type as `Room | undefined` and handle the missing-room path at call sites.
evidence: `initialRoom: Room = rooms[runtime.domain.rooms[0]?.id ?? "server-room"];` assumes the lookup always succeeds, but record indexing can produce `undefined`.

issues.summary: Mission query accumulator is inferred as any[]
issues.suggestion: Declare `result` with an explicit element type matching the returned validator shape (including optional `progressId`) before pushing entries.
evidence: `const result = [];` in `getMissionsWithProgress` creates an `any[]`, so malformed pushes would not be caught until runtime.

issues.summary: Network profile lookup uses key assertion instead of key narrowing
issues.suggestion: Introduce a typed key guard (e.g., `if (sourceRoom in roomNetworkProfiles)`) and narrow before indexing, avoiding `as keyof` assertions.
evidence: `roomNetworkProfiles[sourceRoom as keyof typeof roomNetworkProfiles]` forces compatibility for arbitrary strings, masking invalid key usage.

issues.summary: Internal mutations apply inconsistent ownership checks for player-scoped writes
issues.suggestion: Create a shared internal authorization helper for player-scoped internal writes (for example, validate `gameStateId` ownership and cross-check related record ownership) and apply it uniformly to internal mutations that accept `playerId` or game-state IDs.
evidence: `finalizeCommandOutput` explicitly verifies `outputDoc.playerId === args.playerId` and `gameState.playerId === args.playerId` before patching.

Sibling internal mutations `writeCommandOutput`, `persistCommandGameState`, and `recordToolUsage` patch/insert player-scoped records based only on passed IDs/strings and do not enforce the same ownership invariant.

issues.summary: Internal cache cleanup bypasses admin controls without explicit guardrail/audit pattern
issues.suggestion: Add an explicit privileged-execution contract for internal cleanup paths (for example, dedicated scheduler-only wrapper plus structured audit log mutation for cleanup invocations) so bypass behavior is consistently controlled and observable.
evidence: `cleanupCacheEntries` and `getCacheStats` require `requireAdmin(ctx)`, but `cleanupCacheEntriesInternal` performs the same deletion path with no auth check or audit event.

`cleanupCacheEntriesInternal` directly invokes `internal.utils.cacheUtils.cleanupOldCacheEntries`; no in-code execution constraint (cron-only assertion) or audit logging is enforced at this privileged path.
